answer: An agent economy can deter Sybil attacks via epoch proof-of-burn, requiring each identity to periodically send native tokens to an unspendable address. Just as walnut or saffron carries real scarcity, accounts resist cheap cloning because every renewal destroys irrecoverable capital. Each burn leaves a verifiable on-chain ember that clones cannot reuse. However, token-price volatility weakens this defense: market crashes make Sybil pools cheap, while rallies price out honest newcomers.
